summary: Ported timeout.c:obj_split_timers into js/timeout.js and wired mkobj.c:splitobj to call it before light-source duplication. The exact admitted v79 segment now matches from step 0 through step 284, including the seven lit-candle split and subsequent burn timer handling.

source.branch: mkobj.c:splitobj copies a timed source stack, resets child.timed and child.lamplit, updates ownership, then calls timeout.c:obj_split_timers before obj_split_light_source. The helper saves each timer’s next link before insertion and duplicates every TIMER_OBJECT timer with the same remaining expiry and callback index. JavaScript now follows that order, while retaining the explicit test hook override.
callers: mkobj.c:splitobj is the only direct C caller of timeout.c:obj_split_timers and discards its void result. In gameplay, apply.c:use_candle reaches splitobj while attaching seven lit candles to the Candelabrum; the admitted v79 segment matches through step 284.
dependencies: timeout.c:obj_split_timers calls start_timer and discards the return. The existing js/timeout.js:start_timer implementation inserts the timer and updates object timed counters.
mkobj.c:splitobj calls obj_split_timers before obj_split_light_source. JavaScript retains the optional splitObjectTimers test hook; ordinary production calls use the new source implementation.

selectionReason: Selected the officially admitted v79 lit-candle case after the unchanged-input replay matched 235 screens, cursors, and 2564 RNG calls, then stopped at step 235 with end_burn: lit object has no burn timer.
